claims.text: A machine learning-based computational method can be used to design intrinsically strong refractory HEA compositions.
A machine learning-based computational method can be used to design intrinsically ductile refractory HEA compositions.
A machine learning-based computational method can be used to design low-weight refractory HEA compositions.
The method predicts optimal RHEA compositions using thermodynamic and kinetic principles.
The initial design space consists of multi-principal-element alloys with a very large selection of possible compositions.
The proposed intervention is a machine learning-based computational method for predicting an optimal composition.
The designed RHEAs are intended for high-temperature operating conditions.
Phase stability is the structural mediator connecting composition design to the desired properties.
Thermodynamic and kinetic principles provide the operative design mechanism.
The designed compositions will have 20% greater strength than conventional RHEA compositions.
The designed compositions will have 15% greater ductility than conventional RHEA compositions.
The designed compositions will have 10% lower weight than conventional RHEA compositions.
The permitted composition range is limited to refractory elements.
Machine-learning prediction accuracy may depend on the quality and quantity of training data.
Machine-learning prediction accuracy may be affected by the complexity of the thermodynamic and kinetic principles represented by the model.
